issue.body:
### Issue URL (Incorrect Blocking)
[https://r.bouncycustom.com/](https://adguardteam.github.io/AnonymousRedirect/redirect.html?url=https%3A%2F%2Fr.bouncycustom.com%2F)

### Comment
> **Incorrect adult categorisation on the Family Protection server: bouncycustom.com / r.bouncycustom.com**
> 
> bouncycustom.com and its subdomain r.bouncycustom.com belong to Bouncy (https://bouncy.ai), a link-in-bio and link-management platform used by around 35,000 creators and small businesses. r.bouncycustom.com is a redirect endpoint only: it receives clicks from customers' own custom domains and forwards them to the customer's destination page. It hosts no content of its own (its root page shows only "Routing endpoint").
> 
> **What happens:** on the Family Protection server (family.adguard-dns.com), an A query for r.bouncycustom.com returns 94.140.14.35 instead of the real address 199.36.158.100 (Firebase Hosting). Safari then fails the TLS handshake with the sinkhole and shows "Safari can't open the page because it couldn't establish a secure connection to the server" (first screenshot). The same link works on cellular and on the Default server (second screenshot). bouncy.ai itself resolves normally on the Family server.
> 
> **Impact:** because every custom domain on the platform passes through this one redirect host, the block breaks all ~1,500 customer domains at once, including many non-adult businesses, for anyone on a network that uses the Family server.
> 
> **Why the categorisation is not appropriate:** the host does not serve sexual content. Where a customer's destination is age-restricted, the endpoint shows a plain age-confirmation page before redirecting, and the destination domain itself (for example onlyfans.com) is already categorised independently by the Family filter, so blocking the redirect host adds no protection. Comparable link services (linktr.ee, bit.ly, beacons.ai) resolve normally on the Family server.
> 
> **Request:** please recategorise bouncycustom.com and r.bouncycustom.com as a redirect / link-management service and remove them from the adult category on the Family Protection server.
> 
> Steps to reproduce: set DNS to family.adguard-dns.com, then open https://r.bouncycustom.com/ in any browser.

```
Username: @amaanmuhammad
```


### Screenshots

  <summary>Screenshot 1</summary>

  ![Screenshot 1](https://cdn.adguardcdn.com/sitereports/qzrmhcppx7kk4g4c0gcswwo0k0gooogde9hm28x9rc.jpg?nc=1)
</details>

|-------------|-------|

comment.body:
Apologies for the slow reply, I was away when you answered. Here are custom domains that pass through r.bouncycustom.com and lead to ordinary destinations:

- https://jade.openyoutube.app (YouTube video)
- https://onceplayy.com/max1 (YouTube Shorts)
- https://onceplayy.com/friend-member (YouTube Playables game)
- https://youby.me (WhatsApp business chat)
- https://lacykim.me (TikTok profile)
- https://keloune.com (Instagram profile)
- https://robertadipadua.me (Instagram profile)
- https://thewhiterabbitclub.world (Telegram community)

Each of these is a customer's own domain; the click goes through r.bouncycustom.com and on to the destination. On the Family server all of them fail with a TLS error because the shared redirect host is sinkholed, even though every destination above resolves normally on that server.

To be transparent: a large share of our customers are adult creators, and their destinations (onlyfans.com, fanvue.com, fansly.com) are already blocked by the Family filter on their own domains, so the redirect host adds nothing to protection there. It only breaks the non-adult customers. We would appreciate r.bouncycustom.com and bouncycustom.com being treated like other redirect services (linktr.ee, bit.ly, beacons.ai), which resolve normally on the Family server.
